title: Wrong options that catch the shortcut
statement: Put in wrong options that a shortcut would choose, so that only applying the rule to the new material works.
example: One sorting design added three trap animals, a whale, a jellyfish and a bat, so that the deciding rule and not appearance settles each.
detail: Two Grade 3 designs build the shortcut into the wrong choices. In an inference design, the independent task's wrong words are the reasons from the modelled section, and the feedback on a wrong tap names the difference, so copying the model's answers fails. A classification design adds trap animals whose look points to the wrong group, which force the child to apply the deciding rule over appearance. That the first design aims to catch copying is inferred from its note and its feedback; the second states its aim.
